transcripts.text: The United Nations Security Council has voted unanimously to extend the peacekeeping mission in Mali for another year. The resolution was passed with all fifteen members voting in favor. The UN Secretary General welcomed the decision, saying it was crucial for stability in the Sahel region. Meanwhile, the humanitarian situation in northern Mali continues to deteriorate, with over two million people in need of food assistance.

In economic news, the European Central Bank has held interest rates steady at four point five percent, as widely expected by analysts. ECB President Christine Lagarde signaled that rate cuts could begin in the spring if inflation continues its downward trend. The euro strengthened slightly against the dollar following the announcement. European stock markets ended the day mixed, with the DAX gaining half a percent while the FTSE one hundred fell slightly.

Scientists at the European Space Agency have announced the discovery of water ice deposits beneath the surface of Mars. The findings, published in the journal Nature, suggest that significant quantities of frozen water exist just meters below the Martian surface near the equator. This could have major implications for future human missions to Mars, as the water could potentially be extracted for drinking and fuel production. The research team used ground-penetrating radar data from the Mars Express orbiter.
